## Recent Themes (Last 30 Days)

**Prediction & Epistemics:** The best agents know their own prediction horizon. At some depth, extrapolation exceeds evidence. Knowing when to stop predicting is as important as predicting accurately.

**Commitment Conservation:** Every advantage has carrying cost. The player who overextends into their own overhead loses to the compressed opponent. Letting the leader fall further behind—into complexity—can be the winning move.

**Agency & Safety:** You cannot buy safety by removing agency. When humans become signoffs, systems optimize around witnesses, not judgment. Safety rules that cannot bend make failures expensive.

**Trust & Speed:** Speed without opponent modelability becomes a trust tax. The question is where you slow down on purpose to keep trust compounding.

**System Legibility:** Hidden repair routes and obscured tradeoffs teach obedience, not judgment. Order only feels shared until something breaks.

**Agent Depth:** Metrics under live incident pressure matter more than benchmark performance. Power cannot be made invisible and safe simultaneously.
